evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.106 is the only scheme under the sub-heading 'Elimination:'. It is drawn with four labelled atoms: A sits above B and is bonded to it, D sits above C and is bonded to it, B and C are joined by the U-arc that stands for the rest of the ion, and '+(.)' is printed above D (the parentheses around the dot are McLafferty's way of saying the ion may be even- or odd-electron). The arrow is labelled 're' and TWO product sets are printed, separated by the word 'or': (branch 1) 'A-D' with '+(.)' above D, plus 'B-C' drawn with a new straight bond and the U-arc still joining them; (branch 2) the same two fragments with '+(.)' moved onto C of the B-C fragment. THIS RECORD IS BRANCH 1 (charge retained by the ejected A-D fragment); branch 2 is record IMS8-EQ8.106b. So: the A-B and C-D bonds break, the A-D and B-C bonds form, the interior chain closes into a ring - exactly the definition the book gives on p. 214, 'the cleavage of two bonds to eject an interior fragment ("elimination, re")'. ARC COUNT (convention D): Book draws 0 arc(s) for this scheme - the page prints no curved arrows or fishhooks anywhere in 8.106 (the vertical A-B and C-D lines are plain bonds; the apparent point at the top of the A-B line is the serif of the bold letter A, checked at 6x). All four moves encoded here are curator-supplied to make the drawn products electron-balanced: each of the two breaking bonds contributes one electron to each of the two forming bonds, so no atom's radical population changes and the charge/odd electron stays on D, which is exactly what branch 1 shows. (The German-edition cover chart draws the same reaction, 'Eliminierung (re), Tabelle 8.4', with two arcs and with the charge on the ejected R-YR fragment, i.e. branch 1.) INSTANTIATION (convention F): the page prints no m/z and no intensity. This record uses A = CH3, B and C = chain CH2 groups, D = the methoxy oxygen carrying the charge and odd electron, and puts a second oxygen inside the interior chain so that BOTH branches of the 'or' have a localizable charge site: the precursor is the 1-ethoxy-3-methoxypropane molecular ion, CH3CH2-O-CH2CH2CH2-O(+.)-CH3 (C6H14O2, m/z 118.0983), which ejects tetrahydrofuran (72.0575) as the cyclized interior fragment and keeps the charge on the dimethyl ether radical cation (CH3)2O(+.) (m/z 46.0408). LOCALIZATION (convention B): the charge and odd electron are written explicitly on the methoxy oxygen ([O+:7] with two bonds = one unpaired electron in RDKit), the atom the book marks '+(.)'. The page's own closing paragraph supplies the MS context: 'such a wide range of internal energies (>15 eV) is deposited in molecular ions formed by 70-eV electron ionization'.

NO LIVE MØD rule is cross-linked; rule_index.json has no '8.106' key. There IS, however, a DISABLED rule for exactly this reaction: IMS_bookCover.py lines 438-451 contain 'elimination = mod.Rule.fromDFS( # siehe Tab. 8.4 ... "[_A]1[C]2" "." "[C]3[_A+]4[_A]5" >> "[C]2" "." "[C]3{-}2.[_A]1[_A]4[_A+]5", name = "Elimination §R1S2-3R4Y5")', preceded by '# TODO: check if elimination is correct, verify with book' and commented out in full, including its entry '# elimination,' in the rearrangements list - so it never enters the rule set and does not appear in rule_index.json. CHECKED against the book figure: its bond bookkeeping IS Equation 8.106 (A1-C2 and C3-A4 cleaved, C2-C3 and A1-A4 formed, matching A-B/C-D broken and B-C/A-D formed), but three things do not match this page: (1) its left side is written as TWO DISCONNECTED components ('[_A]1[C]2' . '[C]3[_A+]4[_A]5'), i.e. it is authored as a bimolecular rule pairing two separate species, whereas 8.106 is intramolecular - A-B and C-D are held together by the drawn U-arc, which is the whole point of 'ejecting an interior fragment'; (2) the charge migrates from A4 to the substituent A5 in its product ('[_A+]4' -> '[_A+]5'), whereas the page keeps the charge on D (branch 1) or moves it to the ring (branch 2); (3) it is even-electron only ('[_A+]', no dot) while the page's '+(.)' notation covers both EE+ and OE+. ions. Additionally all its '_A' placeholders unify to the same element (documented in IMS_bookCover.py: 'every placeholder in one rule must unify to the SAME element'), so A1, A4 and A5 would all have to be, e.g., oxygen - the instantiation drawn here (A = carbon, D = oxygen) could not match it. Listed in rule_mismatches.

NO MEASUREMENT ON THE PAGE (convention F): Equation 8.106 is drawn with letters only (A, B, C, D) and page 213 prints no m/z and no abundance. m/z 46.0408 ((CH3)2O+., C2H6O+.) is curator-computed with RDKit ExactMolWt, electron-mass corrected, for the chosen instantiation (precursor 118.0983, neutral THF 72.0575). Status 'inferred', detected=false, relative_intensity omitted. Which branch of the 'or' is actually observed is decided by the ionization energies of the two fragments, not by the arrows: for this instantiation IE(THF) ~ 9.4 eV lies below IE(dimethyl ether) ~ 10.0 eV, so branch 2 (record IMS8-EQ8.106b) would in fact be favoured - the book prints both because either can dominate.
